topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Elastic Collision Framework
lecture_lines: Blocks collide, conserving energy and momentum.
Small mass m, large mass M.
animations: Create two circles, m (small) and M (large), in center #FFFFFF.
Draw velocity vector #00FF00 for m, #FFFF00 for M.
Display m1v1 + m2v2 = constant (#FFFFFF) at top.
Highlight collision impact point with #FF0000 flash using.

sections.title: The Scaling Phenomenon (M = 100^n * m)
lecture_lines: M is 100 to power of n times m.
Collision count equals digits of Pi.
animations: Create one giant rectangle (M) and tiny dot (m).
Display collision counter integer #00FFFF, increment on impact.

sections.title: Geometric Mapping: Phase Space
lecture_lines: Collision system maps to wedge reflection.
Wedge angle determined by mass ratio.
Discrete problem becomes path length problem.
animations: Draw 2D grid (#444444) for velocity coordinates v1, v2.
Plot trajectory line (#FFFFFF) evolving through phase space.
Animate reflecting wedge boundaries (#FF00FF) in the grid.

sections.title: The Limit Case: Why Pi?
lecture_lines: Trajectory unfolds as mass ratio grows.
Zigzag path smooths into circle arc.
Path length reveals ratio of Pi.
animations: Morph trajectory grid to circle arc path #FFFFFF.
Highlight arc curvature #FFFF00 matching the collision path.
Fade in Pi value (3.1415...) #00FF00 near the arc.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Kinetic energy maps to mathematical constants.
Conservation laws bridge physics to geometry.
